chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
I asked him about the ritual bath (ghusl) when throwing the Jamarat (pegs), so he said, 'Perhaps I did it. As for the Sunnah, it is not [obligatory], but [it is done] due to the heat and sweat.'
ai.seo_question: Is the ritual bath after throwing Jamarat obligatory or recommended in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) distinguishes between the legal obligation and the recommended practice of performing ghusl after throwing the Jamarat. He clarifies that while it is not a strict Sunnah in the technical sense, it is a customary practice driven by the physical necessity of relieving heat and sweat, reflecting the practical realities of the Hajj rituals in Medina.
